$comment: The Paga Engine SDK operation dataset. Authored in paga/data, served as paga-<lang>-docs/docs/operations.json.

groups.title: Make payments
groups.description: Send money out to a customer, a biller or a network.

groups.title: Manage accounts
groups.description: Your own account, your customers' accounts, and the customers themselves.

sections.title: Checkout
sections.description: Take a card or bank payment on a Paga-hosted page. The customer is redirected to Paga, pays, and Paga notifies your server.
sections.intro: Checkout is the hosted flow: you send the customer to a Paga page and Paga handles the payment instrument. Use it when you want Paga to own the payment UI rather than building your own.

sections.title: Dynamic virtual account, Bank USSD, Paga wallet and USD bank transfer
sections.description: Collect money from a customer with a payment request. The same request serves the virtual account, USSD, wallet and USD flows — you pick the method.
sections.intro: A payment request tells Paga to collect a specific amount from a specific customer. How the customer pays is up to you: a one-time virtual account number, a USSD prompt, their Paga wallet, or a USD bank transfer.

sections.title: Refunds
sections.description: Refund a payment in full or in part, or cancel one that was never paid.
sections.intro: A refund returns money to the customer. Cancelling a payment request that has not been paid uses the same endpoint — Paga decides which it is from the request's state.

sections.title: Direct Debit (Open Banking)
sections.description: Take a standing authorisation to debit a customer's bank account, then charge against it.
sections.intro: Direct Debit lets a customer authorise you to debit their bank account. You set the mandate up, wait for the bank to approve it, then charge it as often as the mandate allows.

sections.title: Money Transfer
sections.description: Send money out of your business balance to a bank account or a Paga wallet.
sections.intro: A money transfer moves money from your business balance to somebody else. You can validate the destination first, send in bulk, and check the status afterwards.

sections.title: Airtime and data
sections.description: Top up a phone with airtime or a data bundle.
sections.intro: Buy airtime or data for a phone number from your business balance. For data, pick the bundle first — the amount must match the bundle's price exactly.

sections.title: Bill payment (VAS)
sections.description: Pay a biller on behalf of a customer: electricity, water, TV, airtime and more.
sections.intro: Bill payment takes a customer's account number, confirms it with the biller, and pays. Find the biller, pick the service, validate the customer, then pay.

sections.title: Check the transaction status
sections.description: Find out what happened to a money transfer, airtime purchase or bill payment you already sent.
sections.intro: Some operations have no callback. The transaction status endpoint tells you where a transaction got to, and it is what you use to resolve an unknown outcome.

sections.title: Your business account
sections.description: Your own balance, transaction history, merchant onboarding and cash dispensing.
sections.intro: The business account is your own. Read the balance before a payout run, reconcile against the transaction history, and onboard the merchants you aggregate.

sections.title: Subsidiary accounts
sections.description: Paga accounts for your customers, held on your behalf. Issue, hold and move money on their account.
sections.intro: A subsidiary account is a Paga account for one of your customers. You can hold their money, move it between accounts, and set it up to sweep straight into a bank account.

sections.title: Persistent payment accounts
sections.description: A standing instruction that lets a customer pay you repeatedly from the same account.
sections.intro: A persistent payment account is the customer-side equivalent of a direct debit mandate, but from the collection side: the customer authorises a debit, you keep taking it.

sections.title: Customer registration and KYC
sections.description: Open a Paga account for a customer, with identity documents if you need them.
sections.intro: Registering a customer opens a Paga account for them on your business account. The KYC variants upload photographs as well.

operations.name: Verify a charge
operations.operation: Checkout - Verify a charge
operations.description: Confirms a Checkout payment from your server at any time, using its `paymentReference`. Uses HTTP Basic only — it sends no `hash` header.
notes: `status_code` `0` means paid, `2` means pending.
A pending charge is a legitimate answer, so the response is returned rather than raised.

python.example:
verified = await client.verify_charge(
    payment_reference="PAY-2026-0311",
    public_key="YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY",
    amount=50,
)
if verified.status_code == 0:
    print("paid")

operations.name: Create a payment request
operations.operation: Dynamic virtual account - Create a payment request
operations.description: Creates a payment request. The customer pays via the payment methods you send, and Paga calls your callback when the payment completes.
notes: The same operation serves the Bank USSD, Paga wallet and USD bank transfer flows — pick the flow with `paymentMethods`.
`payer.email` takes part in the hash even when you omit it.

python.example:
payment = await client.create_payment(
    reference_number="ORD-2026-0187",
    amount=50,
    payer_name="Bello Ramon",
    payer_phone_number="08064343187",
    payee_name="Your business name",
    payer_email="customer@example.com",
    call_back_url="https://yourstore.com/webhooks/paga",
    payment_methods=["BANK_TRANSFER"],
)

rust.example:
let payment = client
    .create_payment(CreatePayment::new(
        "ORD-2026-0187",
        50.0,
        "Bello Ramon",
        "08064343187",
        "Your business name",
    ))
    .await?;

operations.name: Check payment status
operations.operation: Dynamic virtual account - Check payment status
operations.description: Returns the status of a payment request. The outer `statusCode` only says whether the status request worked; the payment's own status is in `data.statusCode`.
notes: `data.statusCode` of `"0"` means the payment was paid.

operations.name: List the customer's banks
operations.operation: Bank USSD - Get the customer's bank
operations.description: Lists the banks available for a Bank USSD payment. Send a bank's `uuid` as `payer.bankId` when creating a payment request, or as `autoSweep.bankPublicId` for subsidiary accounts.

operations.name: Check USD payment status
operations.operation: Bank transfer (ACH, Wire and Swift) - Check payment status
operations.description: Returns the status of a USD payment request. Unlike the other `/status` operations, this one signs the currency as well as the reference number.
notes: `data.statusCode` of `"1"` means the payment is still pending.

python.example:
status = await client.get_usd_payment_status(
    reference_number="ORD-2026-0187",
    payment_currency="USD",
)

operations.name: Payment request history
operations.operation: Collect API - Payment request history
operations.description: Returns the history of your payment requests.

python.example: history = await client.get_payment_request_history(reference_number="REF-000001")

operations.name: Refund or cancel a payment request
operations.operation: Refunds - Refund or cancel a payment request
operations.description: Refunds a paid payment request in full or in part, or cancels one that has not been paid.
notes: Send one request per partial refund, each with its own `referenceNumber`.
Reusing a `referenceNumber` returns status code `102` and never refunds twice.

python.example:
refund = await client.refund_payment(
    reference_number="RFD-2026-0031",
    payment_request_reference="ORD-2026-0187",
    refund_amount=50,
    reason="Item out of stock",
)

operations.name: Check refund status
operations.operation: Refunds - Check refund status
operations.description: Checks whether a payment request was refunded. Call it with the **original** payment request's `referenceNumber`, not the refund's.
notes: `data.refundStatus` becomes `"refunded"` once the refund is made.

operations.name: Start a hosted set-up session
operations.operation: Direct Debit - Start a hosted set-up session
operations.description: Creates a hosted session and returns the `checkoutUrl` to redirect your customer to. This endpoint uses HTTP Basic only — it sends no `hash` header.
notes: The session expiry and payment expiry are strings of seconds.

python.example:
session = await client.start_direct_debit_session(
    reference_number="DD-2026-0001",
    account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
    amount_limit=50000,
    callback_url="https://yourstore.com/webhooks/mandate",
)
print(session.checkoutUrl)

operations.name: Set up a mandate by API
operations.operation: Direct Debit - Set up a mandate by API
operations.description: Creates a payment request with `paymentMethods` set to `["DIRECT_DEBIT"]`, so the customer authorises you to debit their bank account.
notes: The authorisation transfer must come from mobile banking, internet banking or a branch — not from POS, USSD or ATM.
`payerCollectionFeeShare` and `payeeCollectionFeeShare` must sum to 1.0.

python.example:
mandate = await client.create_direct_debit_mandate(
    reference_number="DD-2026-0001",
    amount=5000,
    payer_name="Bello Ramon",
    payer_phone_number="08064343187",
    payee_name="Your business name",
    account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
    payer_email="customer@example.com",
    call_back_url="https://yourstore.com/webhooks/mandate",
)

rust.example:
let mandate = client
    .create_direct_debit_mandate(CreateDirectDebitMandate::new(
        "DD-2026-0001",
        5000.0,
        "Bello Ramon",
        "08064343187",
        "Your business name",
        "CUST-000184-WALLET",
    ))
    .await?;

operations.name: Check mandate status
operations.operation: Direct Debit - Check mandate status
operations.description: Returns a mandate's status.
notes: `data.statusCode` stays `"1"` / `"pending"` forever — it tells you nothing.
Read `data.additionalData.mandate[].ProcessStatusId` instead: `PENDING`, `VERIFIED`, `APPROVED` or `REJECTED`. Charge only when it is `APPROVED`.

operations.name: Charge the mandate
operations.operation: Direct Debit - Charge the mandate
operations.description: Debits an approved mandate for any amount up to its limit.
notes: A successful response means the charge was **accepted**, not completed — fulfil only once the charge callback confirms it.

python.example:
charge = await client.charge_mandate(
    reference_number="DD-CHARGE-0001",
    amount=600,
    account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
)

operations.name: Check charge status
operations.operation: Direct Debit - Check charge status
operations.description: Returns the status of a mandate charge, using the charge's own `referenceNumber`.
notes: `data.statusCode` is `0` charged, `1` pending, `-1` invalid and `-4` unknown.

operations.name: Disable a mandate
operations.operation: Direct Debit - Disable a mandate
operations.description: Stops all future charges on a mandate. Its `ProcessStatusId` then becomes `REJECTED`, and it can never be charged again.

python.example:
await client.disable_mandate(
    reference_number="DD-DIS-0001",
    account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
)

operations.name: List institutions you can pay
operations.operation: Money transfer - Get the bank's UUID
operations.description: Lists every institution money can be sent to, with the `uuid` you send as `destinationBankUUID`.
notes: UUIDs never change, but new institutions are added every month — cache the list and refresh it weekly or monthly.
To send to a Paga wallet, use Paga's UUID `AAAAAAAA-AAAA-AAAA-AAAA-AAAAAAAAAAAA`.

operations.name: Validate the destination account
operations.operation: Money transfer - Validate the account
operations.description: Confirms the account exists and returns the account holder's name and the fee, before any money moves.
notes: Send `amount` exactly as you will send it later: `"5000.00"` and `"5000"` sign differently.

python.example:
validation = await client.validate_deposit_to_bank(
    reference_number="REF-000002",
    amount="5000.00",
    destination_bank_uuid="40090E2F-7446-4217-9345-7BBAB7043C4C",
    destination_bank_account_number="0000000000",
)
print(validation.destinationAccountHolderNameAtBank, validation.fee)

operations.name: Send money to a bank account
operations.operation: Money transfer - Send the money
operations.description: Sends money from the business balance to a bank account, or to a Paga wallet using Paga's UUID.
notes: Send `amount` as a string (e.g. `"5000.00"`) — it is signed verbatim.
There is no callback for the outcome; use the transaction status endpoint.

python.example:
transfer = await client.send_money(
    reference_number="PAY-2026-0311",
    amount="5000.00",
    destination_bank_uuid="40090E2F-7446-4217-9345-7BBAB7043C4C",
    destination_bank_account_number="0000000000",
    remarks="Salary for June",
)

operations.name: Send money to a Paga wallet
operations.operation: Business API - Money transfer to a Paga wallet
operations.description: Sends money from the business balance to a Paga user, identified by their phone number, nickname or account number.
notes: `referenceNumber` must be at most 50 characters.

python.example:
transfer = await client.transfer_to_paga_wallet(
    reference_number="PAY-2026-0312",
    amount=5000,
    destination_account="08064343187",
)

operations.name: Validate a Paga wallet transfer
operations.operation: Business API - Validate a money transfer
operations.description: Confirms the recipient exists and returns their name, registration status, KYC level and the fee, before any money moves.

python.example:
validation = await client.validate_money_transfer(
    reference_number="REF-000003",
    amount=5000,
    destination_account="08064343187",
)
print(validation.recipientAccountHolderName, validation.fee)

operations.name: Bulk money transfer
operations.operation: Business API - Bulk money transfer
operations.description: Sends up to 300 money transfers in one call.
notes: Paga hashes the **first item's** reference number, amount and destination account, followed by the total number of items — the SDK does that for you.
A bulk transfer can partially succeed, so check every entry in `results`.

operations.name: Check the transaction status
operations.operation: Money transfer / Airtime / Bill payment - Check the transaction status
operations.description: Checks what happened to a transaction you already sent. It covers money transfers, airtime purchases and bill payments.
notes: Only the last 48 hours are covered.
After a timeout or an ambiguous response, wait at least 5 seconds before the first check.
The `status` field is human-readable and may be reworded — branch on `responseCode`, not on `status`.

operations.name: List mobile operators
operations.operation: Airtime and data - Get the mobile operator
operations.description: Lists the networks you can top up.
notes: Send a network's `mobileOperatorCode` as `mobileOperatorPublicId` when buying, and as `operatorPublicId` when listing data bundles.
Cache the list.

operations.name: List data bundles
operations.operation: Airtime and data - For data, pick a bundle
operations.description: Lists a network's data bundles.
notes: Send a bundle's `serviceId` as `mobileOperatorServiceId` and **exactly** its `servicePrice` as `amount`.
Bundles rarely change, so cache the list and refresh it monthly.

python.example:
bundles = await client.get_data_bundles(
    reference_number="REF-000001",
    operator_public_id="42419156-DD57-4737-8373-20678CD9AA29",
)

operations.name: Buy airtime or data
operations.operation: Airtime and data - Buy the airtime or data
operations.description: Tops up a phone with airtime or data from the business balance.
notes: There is no callback: decide on `responseCode`, and check the transaction status if you need to.
For a data bundle, `amount` must be exactly the bundle's `servicePrice`.

python.example:
purchase = await client.buy_airtime(
    reference_number="AIR-2026-0042",
    amount="500",
    destination_phone_number="08063332187",
    mobile_operator_public_id="42419156-DD57-4737-8373-20678CD9AA29",
)

operations.name: List billers
operations.operation: Bill payment - Find the biller
operations.description: Lists every biller, with the `uuid` you send as `merchantAccount`. Cache the list.

operations.name: List a biller's services
operations.operation: Bill payment - Pick the service
operations.description: Lists what a biller can be paid for.
notes: No services means any amount is allowed.
A service with `price` `0.0` means the customer chooses the amount; otherwise pay the service's `price`.

python.example:
services = await client.get_merchant_services(
    reference_number="REF-000001",
    merchant_public_id="A3878DC1-F07D-48E7-AA59-8276C3C26647",
)

operations.name: Validate the customer
operations.operation: Bill payment - Validate the customer
operations.description: Checks a meter, smart card or account number and returns the customer's name.
notes: If the customer chose a service, always send its `code` as `merchantServiceProductCode`.
Billers that don't need it still take part in the hash — send `""` when there is no service.

python.example:
customer = await client.get_merchant_account_details(
    reference_number="REF-000001",
    merchant_account="A3878DC1-F07D-48E7-AA59-8276C3C26647",
    merchant_reference_number="8110411076",
)
print(customer.customerName)

operations.name: Pay the bill
operations.operation: Bill payment - Pay the bill
operations.description: Pays a bill from the business balance.
notes: There is no callback: decide on `responseCode`.
`integrationStatus` is for information only.

python.example:
bill = await client.pay_bill(
    reference_number="BILL-2026-0042",
    amount=6000,
    merchant_account="A3878DC1-F07D-48E7-AA59-8276C3C26647",
    merchant_reference_number="8110411076",
    merchant_service=["STARTERE36"],
)
if bill.responseCode == 0:
    print("paid")

operations.name: Check the business account balance
operations.operation: Your business account - Check your balance
operations.description: Returns the business account balance.
notes: Check `availableBalance`, not `totalBalance`, before a payout run — it is what you can actually send.

python.example:
balance = await client.get_business_balance(reference_number="BAL-2026-0042")
print(balance.availableBalance)

operations.name: Get the transaction history
operations.operation: Your business account - Get your transaction history
operations.description: Returns every transaction on the business account between two dates: money in, money out and fees, up to 10,000 at a time.
notes: Use it to reconcile your records with Paga's.

python.example:
history = await client.get_business_transactions(
    reference_number="HIS-2026-0042",
    start_date_utc="2026-11-01T00:00:00",
    end_date_utc="2026-11-04T00:00:00",
)

operations.name: Get the recent transactions
operations.operation: Your business account - Get your recent transactions
operations.description: Returns the last five transactions on the business account, newest first, without a date range.
notes: For anything further back, use the transaction history endpoint.

python.example: recent = await client.get_recent_transactions(reference_number="REF-000001")

operations.name: Check an operation's status
operations.operation: Business API - Get an operation status
operations.description: Returns the status of a business operation.
notes: The status is in `transactionStatus`, not `status`.

python.example:
status = await client.get_operation_status(reference_number="PAY-2026-0311")
print(status.transactionStatus)

operations.name: Onboard a merchant
operations.operation: Business API - Onboard a merchant
operations.description: Onboards a merchant and returns the credentials Paga issues for it.
notes: For aggregators only.
Paga names the request field `reference`, not `referenceNumber`.

operations.name: Dispense cash
operations.operation: Business API - Dispense cash
operations.description: Dispenses cash against a customer's withdrawal code.

python.example:
cash = await client.dispense_cash(
    reference_number="CASH-2026-0042",
    customer_phone_number="08064343187",
    amount=5000,
    withdrawal_code="123456",
)

operations.name: Create a subsidiary account
operations.operation: Subsidiary Accounts - Create an account
operations.description: Creates a Paga account for one of your customers.
notes: Leave out `autoSweep` for a ledger-backed account that holds funds; set `autoSweep.destination` to `VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT` or `BANK` for a virtual account that settles straight away.
Reusing a `referenceNumber` or `accountReference` returns status code `102` and never creates a second account.

python.example:
account = await client.create_subsidiary_account(
    reference_number="REF-000005",
    account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
    account_name="Bello Ramon",
    iifi_number="22222132329",
    callback_url="https://yourstore.com/webhooks/paga",
)
if account.statusCode == "102":
    print("duplicate reference")

operations.name: Charge a subsidiary account
operations.operation: Subsidiary Accounts - Charge an account
operations.description: Debits a ledger-backed subsidiary account.
notes: Not available on virtual accounts.
Retrying with the same `referenceNumber` never moves money twice.

python.example:
charge = await client.charge_subsidiary_account(
    account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
    reference_number="REF-CHARGE-001",
    amount=1000,
    narration="Service fee",
)
print(charge.newBalance)

operations.name: Top up a subsidiary account
operations.operation: Subsidiary Accounts - Top up an account
operations.description: Credits a ledger-backed subsidiary account from your business balance.
notes: Not available on virtual accounts.

python.example:
top_up = await client.top_up_subsidiary_account(
    account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
    reference_number="REF-TOPUP-001",
    amount=500,
    narration="Bonus credit",
)
print(top_up.newBalance)

operations.name: Transfer between subsidiary accounts
operations.operation: Subsidiary Accounts - Transfer between accounts
operations.description: Moves money between two ledger-backed subsidiary accounts.
notes: Paga sends one callback, for the source account only.

python.example:
transfer = await client.transfer_between_subsidiary_accounts(
    source_account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
    destination_account_reference="CUST-000221-WALLET",
    reference_number="REF-TRANSFER-001",
    amount=1500,
    narration="Payment for goods",
)

operations.name: Retrieve a subsidiary account
operations.operation: Subsidiary Accounts - Retrieve an account
operations.description: Returns an account's details, limits, callback URL and balance.
notes: The `accountIdentifier` is the account's `accountReference`.

python.example:
account = await client.retrieve_subsidiary_account(
    account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
    reference_number="REF-GET-001",
)

operations.name: Update a subsidiary account
operations.operation: Subsidiary Accounts - Update an account
operations.description: Changes an account.
notes: Send only what you want to change.
`accountNumber` and `accountReference` cannot be changed.

python.example:
account = await client.update_subsidiary_account(
    account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
    reference_number="REF-UPDATE-001",
    status="DISABLED",
)

operations.name: Get a subsidiary account balance
operations.operation: Subsidiary Accounts - Get the balance
operations.description: Returns an account's balance.

python.example:
balance = await client.get_subsidiary_balance(
    account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
    reference_number="REF-BAL-001",
)
print(balance.balance)

operations.name: Get a subsidiary account history
operations.operation: Subsidiary Accounts - Get transaction history
operations.description: Returns an account's transactions.
notes: Up to three months at a time.
Pages start at `0`.
`referenceNumber` is required as a query parameter, but is not part of the hash.

python.example:
history = await client.get_subsidiary_history(
    account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
    reference_number="REF-HIS-001",
    start_date_time_utc="2026-06-01T00:00:00",
    end_date_time_utc="2026-06-30T23:59:59",
    page_number=0,
    page_size=20,
)

operations.name: Register a persistent payment account
operations.operation: Collect API - Register a persistent payment account
operations.description: Registers a standing instruction that lets a customer pay you repeatedly from the same account.
notes: `accountReference` must be 11 to 30 characters.
Paga calls your `callbackUrl` whenever the account is funded.

python.example:
account = await client.register_persistent_payment_account(
    reference_number="REF-000006",
    account_reference="CUST-000184-WALLET",
    financial_identification_number="22222132329",
    credit_bank_id="40090E2F-7446-4217-9345-7BBAB7043C4C",
    credit_bank_account_number="0000000000",
    callback_url="https://yourstore.com/webhooks/paga",
)

operations.name: Update a persistent payment account
operations.operation: Collect API - Update a persistent payment account
operations.description: Changes a persistent payment account.
notes: Every field takes part in the hash, so send the current value of the ones you are not changing.

python.example:
account = await client.update_persistent_payment_account(
    reference_number="REF-000007",
    account_identifier="CUST-000184-WALLET",
    callback_url="https://yourstore.com/webhooks/paga-v2",
)

operations.name: Get a persistent payment account
operations.operation: Collect API - Get a persistent payment account
operations.description: Returns a persistent payment account.
notes: The `accountIdentifier` accepts a NUBAN **or** an `accountReference`.

python.example:
account = await client.get_persistent_payment_account(
    reference_number="REF-000008",
    account_identifier="CUST-000184-WALLET",
)

operations.name: Delete a persistent payment account
operations.operation: Collect API - Delete a persistent payment account
operations.description: Deletes a persistent payment account.
notes: The `accountIdentifier` accepts a NUBAN **or** an `accountReference`.

python.example:
await client.delete_persistent_payment_account(
    reference_number="REF-000009",
    account_identifier="CUST-000184-WALLET",
)

operations.name: Register a customer
operations.operation: Business API - Register a customer
operations.description: Opens a Paga account for a customer on your business account.
notes: The phone number must not already belong to a registered customer.

python.example:
customer = await client.register_customer(
    reference_number="REF-000010",
    customer_phone_number="08064343187",
    customer_first_name="Bello",
    customer_last_name="Ramon",
    customer_email="customer@example.com",
    customer_date_of_birth="1989-10-02",
)

operations.name: Register a customer with KYC
operations.operation: Business API - Register a customer with KYC
operations.description: Opens a Paga account for a customer and uploads their identification photographs.
notes: Sent as `multipart/form-data`: a `customer` JSON part, plus `customerAccountPhoto` and `customerIdPhoto` image parts.
Each photograph must be a JPEG of at most 500 KB.

python.example:
with open("account-photo.jpg", "rb") as photo:
    customer = await client.register_customer_with_kyc(
        reference_number="REF-000011",
        customer_phone_number="08064343187",
        customer_email="customer@example.com",
        customer_first_name="Bello",
        customer_last_name="Ramon",
        customer_date_of_birth="1989-10-02",
        customer_gender="MALE",
        customer_account_photo=photo.read(),
        customer_id_photo=photo.read(),
    )

rust.example:
let photo = std::fs::read("account-photo.jpg")?;

let customer = client
    .register_customer_with_kyc(RegisterCustomerWithKyc::new(
        "REF-000011",
        "08064343187",
        "customer@example.com",
        "Bello",
        "Ramon",
        "1989-10-02",
        "MALE",
        photo.clone(),
        photo,
    ))
    .await?;

operations.name: Upload a customer account photo
operations.operation: Business API - Register a customer account photo
operations.description: Uploads a customer's account photograph.
notes: Sent as `multipart/form-data`: a `customer` JSON part plus a `customerAccountPhoto` image part.
The photograph must be a JPEG of at most 500 KB.

python.example:
